belongs_to: Learning Material Sheets, 'Tangram' (pdf p.36, book p.277): 'Note: Cut each shape along the white border.' Pieces lettered A to G; no text of chapter 10 refers to it
description: The seven-piece tangram drawn as one big square (side s, about 752 px on the page picture) made of 7 flat-coloured pieces separated by thin white lines, each piece carrying one white serif capital letter A to G. Page title 'TANGRAM' in pink bubble capitals, line below it 'Note: Cut each shape along the white border.', pink page background, dashed cut line with scissors icons down the left edge. Coordinates below are in units of the side s, origin at the TOP-LEFT corner of the square, x to the right, y downward (centre of the square = (0.5, 0.5)). A (crimson / magenta): large right isosceles triangle on the LEFT, vertices (0,0), (0,1), (0.5,0.5); right angle at the centre; its hypotenuse is the whole left side of the square; area 1/4 of the square; letter A at its middle-left. B (blue): large right isosceles triangle on the TOP, vertices (0,0), (1,0), (0.5,0.5); right angle at the centre; hypotenuse is the whole top side; area 1/4; letter B in its upper middle. E (red-orange): small right isosceles triangle in the TOP-RIGHT corner, vertices (1,0), (1,0.5), (0.75,0.25); right angle at (0.75,0.25); hypotenuse lies along the right side of the square; area 1/16; letter E inside. D (green): square turned 45 degrees (a diamond) to the right of the centre, vertices (0.75,0.25) top, (1,0.5) right, (0.75,0.75) bottom, (0.5,0.5) left; side = about 0.354 s; area 1/8; letter D in its middle. C (light sky-blue / cyan): small right isosceles triangle pointing up, vertices (0.5,0.5) top (right angle at the centre of the big square), (0.75,0.75), (0.25,0.75); its horizontal hypotenuse (length 0.5 s) lies on the line y=0.75; area 1/16; letter C inside. G (orange): parallelogram along the bottom-left, vertices (0.25,0.75), (0.75,0.75), (0.5,1), (0,1): top and bottom sides horizontal and each 0.5 s long (top side from x=0.25 to 0.75, bottom side from x=0 to 0.5), the two slanted sides at 45 degrees leaning to the right; area 1/8; letter G inside. F (purple / violet): medium right isosceles triangle in the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner, vertices (1,1), (0.5,1), (1,0.5); right angle at the bottom-right corner of the square; area 1/8; letter F inside. Piece areas: A 1/4 + B 1/4 + D 1/8 + F 1/8 + G 1/8 + C 1/16 + E 1/16 = 1 (checked). Two large triangles (A, B), one medium triangle (F), two small triangles (C, E), one square (D), one parallelogram (G).

belongs_to: Learning Material Sheets, 'FRACTION WALL' (pdf p.38, book p.279): 'Note: Cut each shape along the white border.' Cut-out fraction strips; no text of chapter 10 refers to it
description: A fraction wall made of 10 vertical strips (columns) standing side by side, all the same width (about 77 px each) and the same total height (about 945 px) and all aligned at the same bottom and top edge, every piece the same flat purple, separated by thin white lines. From left to right the columns are: (1) one single full-height piece labelled '1 UNIT' (the label is printed rotated a quarter turn, reading upward, in the middle of the piece); then columns split into equal pieces with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Column with denominator n has n equal pieces, each 1/n of the full height, so the wall has 1 + (2+3+...+10) = 55 pieces in all (verified by counting the white dividing lines in each column: n-1 per column). Every fraction label is a printed stacked fraction (numerator over a bar over denominator) rotated a quarter turn counter-clockwise, placed at the TOP end of its piece. Labels from the bottom piece upward are k/n: the piece at the bottom of the column is 1/n, the next one up is 2/n, and so on, and the topmost piece is n/n (a full unit). Column contents (top to bottom): denominator 2 (2 pieces, top to bottom: 2/2, 1/2); denominator 3 (3 pieces, top to bottom: 3/3, 2/3, 1/3); denominator 4 (4 pieces, top to bottom: 4/4, 3/4, 2/4, 1/4); denominator 5 (5 pieces, top to bottom: 5/5, 4/5, 3/5, 2/5, 1/5); denominator 6 (6 pieces, top to bottom: 6/6, 5/6, 4/6, 3/6, 2/6, 1/6); denominator 7 (7 pieces, top to bottom: 7/7, 6/7, 5/7, 4/7, 3/7, 2/7, 1/7); denominator 8 (8 pieces, top to bottom: 8/8, 7/8, 6/8, 5/8, 4/8, 3/8, 2/8, 1/8); denominator 9 (9 pieces, top to bottom: 9/9, 8/9, 7/9, 6/9, 5/9, 4/9, 3/9, 2/9, 1/9); denominator 10 (10 pieces, top to bottom: 10/10, 9/10, 8/10, 7/10, 6/10, 5/10, 4/10, 3/10, 2/10, 1/10). Because the pieces of a column are equal slices of the same height, piece boundaries of different columns line up where fractions are equal (for example the top of 1/2 is level with the tops of 2/4, 3/6, 4/8 and 5/10, and the top of every n/n piece is level with the top of the 1 UNIT piece). Page: lavender background, title 'FRACTION WALL' in purple bubble capitals, a note line, dashed cut line with scissors icons down the left edge.

belongs_to: Learning Material Sheets, two-colour tile sheet (pdf p.40, book p.281): 'Note: Cut the tiles along the white border.' Cut-out tiles; no text of chapter 10 refers to it
description: A sheet of 88 identical square tiles in 8 columns x 11 rows (counted and checked tile by tile), each tile about 97 px square on the page picture, separated by white lines. Every tile is cut by one diagonal running from its BOTTOM-LEFT corner to its TOP-RIGHT corner into two right isosceles triangles: the UPPER-LEFT triangle is light blue and the LOWER-RIGHT triangle is yellow. All 88 tiles have exactly the same orientation and colours (no rotated, mirrored or swapped tiles), so each tile is half blue and half yellow. Page: peach background, the line 'Note: Cut the tiles along the white border.' above the sheet, dashed cut line with scissors icons down the left edge. No numbers or letters on the tiles.
